geology: Primary hypogene copper-iron sulfide; the most abundant copper ore mineral, found in porphyry and volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits.
extraction: Pyrometallurgical: concentrate smelted to copper matte, converted to blister copper, fire-refined to anode, then electrorefined to cathode. Se/Te/Au/Ag recovered from anode slimes; S captured as sulfuric acid; Mo recovered as molybdenite from flotation.
notes: Dominant global copper source. Cross-links: principal industrial source of Se and Te; significant Au/Ag and Mo byproducts.

geology: Copper-iron sulfide ('peacock ore'); hypogene and supergene enrichment zones of porphyry copper deposits.
extraction: Pyrometallurgical smelting-converting-refining route, as for chalcopyrite.
notes: Higher Cu content than chalcopyrite. Often intergrown with chalcocite in enriched zones.

geology: Secondary copper sulfide formed by supergene enrichment above the water table; high-grade copper mineral.
extraction: Pyrometallurgical (smelt/convert/refine) for concentrate; supergene/secondary ore also amenable to acid heap leach + SX-EW.
notes: High theoretical Cu (~80%). Leaches more readily than chalcopyrite, so often feeds SX-EW.

geology: Secondary copper sulfide of supergene enrichment zones; usually subordinate to chalcocite.
extraction: Pyrometallurgical route; or acid leach + SX-EW for oxidized/secondary ore.
notes: Minor relative to chalcopyrite/chalcocite but a recognized supergene copper mineral.

geology: Green copper carbonate hydroxide; supergene oxidized zone of copper deposits, with azurite, cuprite and native copper.
extraction: Hydrometallurgical: dilute sulfuric acid heap/vat leach to PLS, solvent extraction to upgrade/purify, electrowinning to cathode (SX-EW).
notes: Acid-soluble oxide ore; little to no precious-metal byproduct. ~57% Cu theoretical.

geology: Blue basic copper carbonate; supergene oxidized zone, commonly altering to malachite.
extraction: Hydrometallurgical acid leach to PLS, then SX-EW.
notes: Formula also written 2CuCO3.Cu(OH)2. Acid-soluble oxide ore.

geology: Copper(I) oxide; oxidized zone of copper lodes, associated with native copper, malachite, azurite and iron oxides.
extraction: Hydrometallurgical acid leach to PLS, then SX-EW.
notes: Very high Cu (~88%). Minor but readily leachable oxide ore.

geology: Metallic copper in basalt amygdules and oxidized zones; historically a major source (e.g. Michigan Keweenaw).
extraction: Physical concentration then direct melting and fire/electro refining; no chemical reduction needed.
notes: Already metallic; may carry native silver.

formula: rock: gibbsite Al(OH)3 + boehmite AlO(OH) + diaspore AlO(OH)
geology: Lateritic/karst weathering residue; not a single mineral but a mix of hydrous aluminium oxides with iron oxides, silica and titania.
extraction: Bayer process: hot caustic NaOH digestion (higher T for boehmite/diaspore), clarification (red mud residue), precipitation and calcination to smelter-grade alumina; then Hall-Heroult electrolysis of alumina dissolved in molten cryolite with carbon anodes to primary aluminium.
notes: Bauxite is a ROCK, not a formula. Energy-intensive. Gibbsite digests easiest; diaspore hardest. Red mud is the major residue; Ga recovered from Bayer liquor.

geology: Lead sulfide; the dominant primary lead ore (86.6% Pb), in hydrothermal veins and Pb-Zn-Ag (e.g. SEDEX, MVT) deposits.
extraction: Sinter-roasting oxidizes PbS to PbO sinter (SO2 to acid); sinter reduced with coke in a lead blast furnace (or Imperial Smelting Furnace, co-producing zinc) to lead bullion; refined (Parkes desilvering, etc.).
notes: Silver is the major byproduct and often the economic driver. Cross-links: leading silver source; coupled to zinc via ISP.

geology: Zinc sulfide (ZnS with Fe substitution); the primary zinc ore (~95% of primary zinc), in Pb-Zn-Ag hydrothermal, SEDEX and MVT deposits.
extraction: RLE (dominant, ~85%+): roast concentrate to ZnO calcine (SO2 to sulfuric acid), leach calcine in spent sulfuric electrolyte, purify (cement out Cu/Cd/Co), electrowin zinc onto aluminium cathodes. Minority pyrometallurgical ISP route.
notes: Cross-links: THE dominant source of Cd, In and Ge (tech metals), plus Ga. Pb/Ag report to residues in mixed ores.

geology: Zinc carbonate; secondary mineral in oxidized zones of zinc deposits ('dry bone' / calamine).
extraction: Calcination to ZnO then acid leach, purification and electrowinning (fed into the hydromet circuit); or pyrometallurgical reduction.

geology: Zinc silicate; oxidized zone of zinc deposits, also called calamine with smithsonite.
extraction: Acid leach, solution purification, then electrowinning.
notes: Silicate oxide ore; requires silica management in the leach circuit.

geology: Tin(IV) oxide; the only significant tin ore (78.8% Sn), in granite-associated hard-rock veins/greisens and alluvial (placer) deposits.
extraction: Gravity concentration exploits high SG (~7); magnetic separation rejects Fe/W minerals. Concentrate reduced by two-stage carbothermic smelting with coal/coke, then thermal/electrolytic refining.
notes: Dense and inert, so gravity-concentrated (placers need little grinding). Hard-rock concentrates may carry Nb/Ta/W byproducts.
